stimulus.text: Paraphrase: From April to June 1945, delegates from 50 nations met in San Francisco to write the charter of a new world organization. On June 26, 1945, they signed the United Nations Charter, which set out the purposes of the United Nations: to keep the peace, to settle disputes without war, and to encourage cooperation among nations. The Charter came into force on October 24, 1945, once enough nations, including the United States, had ratified it. The United States Senate approved the Charter by a wide margin, and the United States became a founding member.
stimulus.source_note: Original secondary summary of the San Francisco Conference and the United Nations Charter, April to June 1945. Dates verified against the United Nations Charter record: signed June 26, 1945; in force October 24, 1945.

source: original; stimulus drawn from book-grounded paraphrases, tables, and photographs (see source_note)
stem: What did the delegates at San Francisco create in June 1945?

options.text: The League of Nations, to replace the United Nations
options.misconception: The League of Nations had ended with the war; San Francisco created its replacement.

options.text: The Bretton Woods system of international lending
options.misconception: Bretton Woods was agreed in New Hampshire in July 1944, a year earlier.

options.text: A military alliance against the Soviet Union
options.misconception: The Soviet Union was a founding member of the United Nations, not its target.

options.text: The United Nations, to keep the peace among nations

rationales.A: Background from the books: the League of Nations had ended with the war; San Francisco created its replacement.
rationales.B: Background from the books: Bretton Woods was agreed in New Hampshire in July 1944, a year earlier.
rationales.C: Background from the books: the Soviet Union was a founding member of the United Nations, not its target.
rationales.D: The delegates signed the United Nations Charter on June 26, 1945, creating an organization to keep the peace and settle disputes without war.
rationales.general:
1. The stimulus says delegates from 50 nations met in San Francisco from April to June 1945.
2. On June 26 they signed the United Nations Charter.
3. The Charter set out the purposes of the new organization: to keep the peace and settle disputes without war.
4. Background: the Charter came into force on October 24, 1945, once enough nations had ratified it.
Remember: a charter is a founding document, and its signing date marks the birth of the organization.
